question: When you pick up a tool that cannot paint inside a marquee, what should happen to the outline you drew?
context: Today, drawing a marquee and then pressing R (rectangle) makes the outline vanish, the Selection X/Y/W/H section disappears from the panel, and Command Z does nothing about it: it steps to your last edit to the picture instead. Reproduced in the app on 2026-09-08. Option A was also built and photographed before filing, so both pictures in the brief are the real app.

options.label: It stays up
options.summary: The outline stays on the canvas whatever tool you pick up, and its X, Y, W and H stay in the panel. Draw a rectangle, take a measurement, come back to the marquee tool, and the outline is exactly where you left it. Only you clear it, by clicking bare canvas or pressing Escape.
pros: Nothing you placed by hand ever disappears without you asking
Matches Photoshop, where the outline survives every tool trip
The panel keeps showing the numbers, so you can keep lining the box up while you work
cons: The dashed outline is on screen while you draw, and a shape you draw is not confined to it, so the outline is not telling you anything about the next stroke
options.mitigation: The outline is thin black and white dashes and the thing you are drawing gets a blue outline with handles, so the two never read as the same object. Photoshop has had exactly this for thirty years and people use the leftover outline as a landmark, not a promise.

options.label: It goes, and one undo brings it back
options.summary: Picking up a paint tool still clears the outline, but it becomes a real step: press Command Z once and the outline is back, along with the tool you were holding when you drew it. Press Command Z again and you are back to your last edit to the picture.
pros: The screen stays quiet: no dashes while you draw
Nothing is lost for good, which is the actual complaint
Redo puts you back in the paint tool
cons: Undo now has to hand back your tool as well as your outline, so one press can change two things at once, which is more surprising than it sounds
options.mitigation: Undo already hands your tool back after a paste, so the app has taught this move once already.

options.label: It waits out of sight
options.summary: The outline is kept but hidden while a paint tool is in hand. Pick up the pointer or the marquee tool again and it fades back in exactly where it was. Command Z is never spent on it.
pros: Quiet screen while you draw, and nothing is lost
Undo stays purely about the picture
cons: An outline that is invisible but still live is a hidden mode: you would reasonably think it was gone, and then it reappears
options.mitigation: A brief note the first time it comes back, saying the outline was kept.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.summary: Picking up a paint tool keeps clearing the outline for good, and Command Z keeps stepping over it to your last edit to the picture.
cons: One stray press of a tool letter still throws away an outline you spent time placing, with nothing to bring it back
options.mitigation: None. This is the behaviour the report is about.
